Dress Up reports · ^du_report(16) · 2026-10-21 · work in progress · about Messed Up Dress Up, a game made with M and N · after ^du_report(15)

The Space Between the Boxes

About 12 minutes to read (2,910 words, not counting tables and figures).

Every panel is boxed now. How much of each panel is empty, between its boxes and inside them, at the screens and zoom levels the game is played on? Where does that space come from, and how much can the layout give back without hiding what a player uses? The follow-up to ^du_report(5), “Always Be Knolling”, from ^ticket(521). Matthew, 2026-10-21 14:00: “The prior effort created panels that leave a lot of "whitespace" between them in common zoom levels and screen sizes. Do an audit of that for the new report, and try to reduce that (before vs after) with a PR that we plan to merge with improvements.”

Short answers. Measured in Chrome on GitHub's computers by knoll521, three jobs each measuring the builds side by side ([3]); “empty between boxes” is the share of a panel covered by no box and no loose control or text, the mean over every tab and place measured.

  1. Full screen is where the space is. At 1920×1080, main (0.0.405) leaves 62.3% of the boxes' side of the full screen empty between boxes; after c10, 53.3%. At 0.0.204 only 🎵 Music and 🗺️ World design had a full screen (37.8%); on those two alone, main reads 44.0% and after 44.0%.
  2. The side panel is less empty than at 0.0.204, and less again after. Side panel 1920×1080: 43.7% at 0.0.204, 37.7% on main, 27.1% after. At 1366×768: 37.8%, 27.9%, 21.9%. iPad portrait full screen: 26.6%, 30.4%, 21.2%.
  3. Where it comes from (read in the code, and seen in the box maps of Figure 3): empty columns (a grid of 4 columns holding 1 or 2 boxes), the hole under a short box beside a tall one, and the game's card in full screen, which left its column mostly empty. The side panel sits on the 568 px line between one and two columns at the common laptop zooms (the zoom).
  4. Four bugs found on the way, fixed in the branch's second commit (found); one of the fixes, Background's side panel as a grid, made that panel longer and emptier at every place measured; packing the boxes (c5) then made it shorter than on main (at 1920×1080, 2.92 → 2.65 windows tall), though with gaps between its boxes its empty share stays higher (5.7% → 19.6%) (each commit).
  5. The panels grew by half since ^du_report(5): 1,548 → 2,293 rows declared, 107 → 132 groups, 61 boxes planned in TAB_BOXES (none at 0.0.204).
  6. The measure repeats. In this run (out3) 3,960 cases were measured in two jobs or more; all but 4 agree to the pixel. Those 4 are the bubble room's full screen, where the jobs differ by up to 0.02 points (672 px²): most likely because its bubbles move. Outside the bubble room the noise floor is 0.

How the space is measured

  • A box is found by its look, not its class: a border on three sides, or a tint of its own, holding a control or text. So the same check reads 0.0.204, main and the branch.
  • Empty between boxes is the share of the panel's whole length covered by no box (each widened by 4 px, so the 8 px gutter does not count) and by no loose control or text. In full screen only the boxes' side is measured, left of the split. Empty inside boxes is the share of each box's content covered by no control and no line of text (each widened by 3 px).
  • Zoom by the device scale factor, as Chrome's zoom and a 125% or 150% display do: the page is laid out at the screen's size divided by the zoom, so media queries, the 568 px line and the minimum split react as on a zoomed screen. Every case asserts a 16 px root font. Screens are named in device pixels; the widths in this report are CSS pixels.
  • Before and after on one machine. The workflow [4] serves every build side by side from git worktrees: 0.0.204 (job 1 only, with the screenshots), main, and every commit of the branch knoll-521 [5]; each job measures them in a different order. Commits in between are shared out across the jobs, at 4 screens. Before each load the page's saved storage is cleared.
  • A self-test first: a page with a known hole, 300×196 of 600×300 = 32.7%, must read exactly that. Job 1 printed: “the instrument: a known hole (300 x 196 of 600 x 300 = 32.7%) read as such”.
  • The machine: Chrome/155.0.8059.39, AMD EPYC 9V74 80-Core Processor, Ubuntu 24.04; fonts DejaVu Sans Book, Noto Color Emoji Regular. Not the kids' fonts, so this report compares builds with each other, not with what M and N see.

Not every commit empties less everywhere. The commit that gave 🏞️ Background's side panel a grid with gaps (the fourth of the four bugs) made the side panel of every place measured both longer and much emptier, as the list above shows; most likely because, two to a row, a short box stands beside a long one, the hole that packing the boxes is meant to fill.

Report 5's rules, amended

  • Rule 3, split. Things of a kind stay in rows (cards, theme cards, music cards, mixer strips, the castle designer's rooms, the world's order); different things, the boxes of a tab, are packed, each under the one above it, with no hole under a short one.
  • Rule 4, extended. A row of chips is a row too: a short row of chips (8 or fewer) sits beside its label in a box wide enough, and a row that would take 3 lines or more is a chip box (the next rule).
  • Rule 8, made exact. The same at every width and zoom: the measure is the side panel at 1366x768 and 1920x1080 at 100%, 125% and 150%, the iPad both ways, and the phone, as tools/checks/knoll521.mjs measures it.
  • New: no empty column. A grid has no more columns than boxes; what a full screen does not need for boxes, the game's card takes.
  • New: a long choice is one chip. Twelve or more text choices are one chip naming the current one, opening ticket ^ticket(459)'s chip box (✖ and Escape close it); no dropdowns.

Found on the way

  • fitPic did not know the generic full screen's card. 21-size-and-divider.js: in the 17 generic full screens the picture was not fitted to its card, so it was letterboxed (Figure 6). Fixed in the PR, the commit named "four panel bugs".
  • The bubble room's settings landed in a box named "🏰 the castles". 22-full-screen.js: the test picking the castles' box matched "room"; now it picks keys and groups that start with "castle". Same commit.
  • 🔬 and ♿ stopped laying their switches out as chips. style.css: the rules for 🔬 Inspection's and ♿ Accessibility's chips did not reach through the designer's wrapper, one version after they shipped (0.0.315). Same commit.
  • Background's side panel had boxes but no grid. the boxes touched, with no gap between them; now a grid with the box gap, two to a row from 568 px. Same commit.
  • The bubble room's full screen is not the same twice. the only case where the three jobs differ (Figure 2's note): most likely because its bubbles move and the measure catches them in different places (not confirmed). Every other case, in every build, agrees to the pixel.

How this was put together

Written on 2026-10-21 by Claude, for Matthew, from ^ticket(521). The panels were read in the code at main and counted in node [6]; the space was measured by knoll521 [3] on GitHub, runs out (3 jobs, builds v204, main, c1), out2 (3 jobs, builds v204, main, c1, c2, c3, c4), out3 (3 jobs, builds v204, main, c1, c2, c3, c4, c5, c6, c7, c8, c9, c10); this page is drawn from out3. Nothing was measured on the laptop, and no browser drew this page while it was made: it was built and checked with python (well-formed, every figure drawn, every link a file).

The data: data/report.json, data/whitespace.json (every case of the run: its share, holes, boxes, the picture's size; and each earlier run's means and noise), data/counts.json, all embedded in this page; on GitHub, data and drivers. drivers/gather.py reads the runs, drivers/build.py draws the page. The picture at the top of the series index is the castle with the friend, from the picture archive [7], the place with the longest Background panel (69 rows).
